title: Trim three overgrown shoots off a box hedge with hedge shears, without cutting the flowers
instruction: Trim the three tall green shoots off the box hedge with the hedge shears, cutting each just above the hedge, without cutting the flowers. Then leave the shears lying closed on the mat and take both arms back to where they started.
context: Gardeners trim hedges with two-handed hedge shears: each blade is worked by its own handle, so the blades open and close only when both handles are moved against each other, and the cut has to miss the plants that should stay.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A dark green-grey rubber mat 3 mm thick, from 11 to 44 cm forward and from 16 cm right to 16 cm left of the centre line, fixed. (2) Lying closed on the mat, pointing forward, a pair of hedge shears (two halves of 0.22 kg each, 42 cm long overall), their pivot bolt 36 cm forward on the centre line: two forged steel blades 4 mm thick and 17 cm long (3.4 cm wide at the heel, tapering to a rounded 1.9 cm tip) lying one on the other, joined by a steel pivot bolt with a brass nut that turns freely; each blade is one piece with a steel tang, a steel ferrule and an octagonal ash handle 16 cm long, 1.9 cm wide and 2.4 cm deep, ending 25 cm from the pivot; the handles splay 28 degrees either side of the blades' line (56 degrees apart with the blades closed), and black rubber bumpers on the tangs meet when the blades are closed. (3) A cedar planter trough 15 cm front to back, 35 cm wide and 5 cm tall, from 55.5 to 70.5 cm forward and centred on the centre line, filled with soil, fixed. (4) In it a clipped box hedge 12 cm front to back and 31.6 cm wide, its top 9.5 cm above the table. (5) Three overgrown shoots, fresh green stems 7 mm thick with young leaves, growing out of the front of the hedge 58.5 cm forward, at 7.5 cm left, on and 7.5 cm right of the centre line, their tips 21.5 cm above the table (12 cm above the hedge). (6) Two flowers in the back row of the hedge, 66.5 cm forward and 3.75 cm left and right of the centre line: a pink and an orange bloom 3.8 cm across on 4 mm green stems, 17.5 cm above the table. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged from the whole trial. A shoot is trimmed when the shears sever it within 1.8 cm of its cut height (2 cm above the hedge); a flower is cut when the shears sever it anywhere along its stem above the hedge. In a real trial severing is observed directly: the stem's top comes away. In the simulation, where blades do not sever stems by contact, a stem counts as severed when the blades, open at least 20 degrees with the stem between them 2.5 to 15 cm from the pivot, close to 6 degrees open or less while it is still there; its top is then freed and falls. A severed stem stays severed. The shears lie closed on the mat when their pivot is over the mat (at least 2 cm in from its edges), no more than 1.2 cm higher than when they lie flat, the blades within 10 degrees of level and open 6 degrees or less. 0.0 once either flower has been cut. Otherwise 1.0: all three shoots cut, the shears lying closed on the mat and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start), at the end; 0.5: all three shoots cut; 0.25: at least one shoot cut; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the shears still.
reset_notes: Put three fresh shoots back in the front of the hedge, check the two flowers are whole, and lay the shears closed on the mat, pointing forward.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: stems are not severed by contact; nothing collides with them below their cut height and the blades pass through them. Severing is approximated by the blades opening 20 degrees round a stem and closing to 6 degrees on it, which frees its top to fall; a real trial observes severing directly. Each half of the shears has its centre of mass on its handle, 16 cm from the pivot. Mat, planter and hedge are fixed.
